title: Human-AI collaborative generative AI for comfortable care: a doctor–patient–AI feedback loop for pre-operative distress and workforce shortages
abstract: Psychological screening is easily displaced by physiological safety checks when preoperative teams have little time and too few staff. Healthcare systems are already affected by widespread workforce shortages and clinician burnout. We suggest that preoperative anxiety consequently often remains unmanaged, with implications for postoperative recovery and hospital workload. Generic educational materials do not adequately address differences in patients’ anxiety, and “health data poverty” can further exclude vulnerable groups. We propose a conceptual human-machine collaborative (HMC) generative artificial intelligence framework to address these clinical and occupational problems together. In the proposed doctor–patient–AI feedback loop, natural language processing would dynamically assess psychosocial risk and guide patient-specific, multimodal education, including dialect-adapted voice agents, as a source of baseline emotional support. Routine interactions would be automated under clinician supervision. Our hypothesis is that this arrangement may conserve clinicians’ limited emotional bandwidth and allow healthier “cognitive reappraisal” in place of chronic fatigue. Implementation science provides a basis for considering how lightweight AI models could be scaled across regional health networks to bring standardized psychoeducation to under-resourced rural areas. This remains a theoretical pathway. Through sociotechnical governance and “data solidarity” to fairly manage algorithmic liability, the framework is still a conceptual framework, but it is operational: it proposes a path to improve perioperative workflows and health equity in the face of severe human resource constraints.
authors: Hui Sun, Yan Luan, Bo Song

title: Cross-linguistic differences in responses to patient queries on osteonecrosis of the femoral head between English and Chinese-oriented large language models: a semantically matched bilingual cross-sectional study
abstract: BackgroundLarge language models (LLMs) are capable of providing health information and consultation to patients with osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH). However, owing to imbalances in the linguistic distribution of their training corpora, the quality, readability, and safety profiles of outputs generated by the same model may vary across language settings.ObjectiveThis study aimed to compare bilingual responses to ONFH patient queries generated by six state-of-the-art flagship LLMs, comprising three English-oriented models (ChatGPT-5.6-Sol, Gemini-3.1-Pro, and Claude-Fable-5) and three Chinese-oriented models (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Qwen3.7-Max, and Doubao-Seed-2.1-Pro), and to multidimensionally evaluate their cross-linguistic capabilities for generating medical information in terms of information quality, actionability, clinical accuracy, safety risk, hallucination, and readability.MethodsA question set comprising 36 semantically distinct patient queries regarding ONFH was developed, yielding 72 semantically matched English–Chinese paired prompts. Six state-of-the-art flagship LLMs were evaluated. Information quality was assessed using the Global Quality Score (GQS), DISCERN, the Quality Assessment of Medical Artificial Intelligence (QAMAI), and the 20-item Ensuring Quality Information for Patients (EQIP-20). Actionability was assessed using the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials (PEMAT-P), while clinical accuracy was evaluated using a 5-point Likert scale. Safety risk was assessed using a graded classification framework, and prespecified criteria were established for identifying hallucinations. Readability was evaluated using language-specific readability metrics for English and Chinese responses. Statistical analyses included the Friedman test, paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and Spearman correlation analysis.ResultsA total of 432 responses generated by LLMs were included in this study, and good-to-excellent inter-rater reliability was observed for all evaluation indicators. Significant between-model differences in actionability and clinical accuracy were identified among the six models under both English and Chinese response conditions (all p < 0.05). Furthermore, clinical accuracy exhibited high cross-linguistic stability. ChatGPT-5.6-Sol showed high actionability and a relatively low frequency of Level 1 minor safety-related omissions under the English-language condition, whereas switching to Chinese was accompanied by reduced actionability and an increased frequency of Level 1 omissions. All observed nonzero safety events were Level 1 minor omissions; no Level 2 or Level 3 unsafe responses were identified in either language condition. Responses generated by all six models in both languages failed to reach the prespecified readability threshold for patient education.ConclusionThe six LLMs showed significant inter-model differences in the actionability and clinical accuracy of responses to ONFH-related patient health queries in both English and Chinese settings, while clinical accuracy demonstrated favorable cross-linguistic stability. Notably, none of the six-model outputs met the applicable readability threshold for patient-targeted health education under either language condition. In clinical practice, model selection, prompting-language effects and hallucination-related risks should be comprehensively considered when deploying LLMs to deliver health information for patients with ONFH. At the present stage, LLM-generated content intended for direct patient-facing education requires cautious evaluation and human oversight.
authors: ShiHang Cao, JiaChen Liang, HaiNing Zhang, et al.

title: Experiences of maternal distress and early childhood development amid climate-related stress in Benue state, Nigeria: a qualitative study
abstract: BackgroundClimate-related flooding and extreme heat affect maternal and child wellbeing in low-and middle-income countries. Although evidence suggests that climate-related events can affect mental health and child wellbeing, little is known about how these experiences are described in flood-prone settings. This study explores participants’ accounts of flooding, extreme heat, and household vulnerability in Benue State and their perceived implications for maternal mental health and early childhood development.MethodsA qualitative descriptive design was used. Data were collected through six focus group discussions and six semi-structured interviews with 54 mothers, health workers, community leaders, and policymakers and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.ResultsParticipants described flooding as a recurrent threat shaped by spatial vulnerability, poor drainage, and inadequate land-use planning. Participants described flooding in relation to disrupted routines, livelihoods, food and water security, and caregiving; mothers and health workers also described extreme heat as disrupting sleep and caregiving. Participants described maternal psychological distress associated with uncertainty, household disruption, economic losses, and caregiving demands. Participants described challenges affecting children’s nutrition, healthcare access, immunisation, learning, safety, and social development. Community coping strategies included collective action and social support, while participants described gaps in formal responses.ConclusionThe findings highlight interconnected experiences of climate-related disruption, maternal distress, caregiving, and conditions relevant to early childhood wellbeing. Responses could support continuity of health services, nutrition, early learning, safe environments, psychosocial support, and community participation.
authors: Ngozi Idemili-Aronu, John Jemisenia, Deborah Aluh, et al.

title: Associations of multimorbidity burden with healthcare utilization and expenditures among individuals with diabetes in China
abstract: ObjectiveMultimorbidity is common among people with diabetes, but its associations with healthcare utilization and medical expenditures in China remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to examine these associations using different measures of multimorbidity burden and assess potential sex differences.MethodsWe conducted cross-sectional analyses using the 2018 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) and a retrospective hospital-based cohort. Multimorbidity burden was assessed using four measures: multimorbidity, ≥3 LTCs, number of long-term conditions (LTCs), and the Chinese Multimorbidity-Weighted Index (CMWI). Multivariable regression models were used to examine associations with healthcare utilization and expenditures. Sex-stratified analyses, interaction tests, and sensitivity analyses were also performed.ResultsAmong 2,531 CHARLS participants with diabetes, 92.9% had multimorbidity and 77.7% had ≥3 LTCs. All four measures were positively associated with inpatient and outpatient utilization, visit counts, and medical expenditures. The presence of ≥3 LTCs was associated with higher odds of inpatient (OR, 2.44; 95% CI, 1.90–3.16) and outpatient utilization (OR, 2.17; 95% CI, 1.68–2.84), as well as higher total inpatient (cost ratio, 2.98; 95% CI, 1.94–5.24) and outpatient expenditures (cost ratio, 3.15; 95% CI, 1.92–5.72). In the hospital cohort (n = 3,963), all four measures were positively associated with hospitalization frequency, cumulative inpatient days, and inpatient expenditure. Most sex interaction tests were not statistically significant. Sensitivity analyses yielded generally consistent findings.ConclusionGreater multimorbidity burden was associated with higher healthcare utilization and medical expenditures among individuals with diabetes across two different settings. These findings highlight the importance of considering coexisting conditions in healthcare planning.
authors: Jielong Wu, Bo Li, Xuemin Wu, et al.

title: Domain Adaptation of a Large Language Model for Radiology Impression Generation – Multi-Reader Evaluation
abstract: To evaluate the clinical and practical trade-offs between domain adaptation and fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) for radiology impression generation, with outcomes assessed through blinded expert radiologist review. In this retrospective institutional review board (IRB)-approved study 3,123,836 CT and MR reports were split into domain adaptation (80%), fine-tuning (16%), validation (2%), and test (2%) sets. Five LLM models were compared to ground truth: a base Llama-3-8B model (Meta) domain-adapted with mixed general, medical, and radiology text then fine-tuned using small ( n = 1,280) and large ( n = 499,814) number of report-impression pairs (DA + FTs, DA + FTl), an OpenBio-8B model with identical fine-tuning (Bio + FTs, Bio + FTl) and Gemini-1.5-Flash-002 used out-of-the-box. Four radiologists independently rated generated radiology impressions for abdominal CT and MR reports using six 5-point Likert items. Automated NLP metrics were also assessed. A Controlled Single-Speaker Evaluation of Ambient Voice Technologies’ Speech-to-Text Function Using Narrated Surgical Case-Reports
abstract: Ambient voice technologies (AVT) utilise automatic speech recognition (ASR) and generative artificial intelligence for speech-to-text conversion, and are advocated as efficient, accurate tools for clinical documentation. We investigated ( n = 8) AVT systems using surgical case-reports as narratives in a controlled single-speaker evaluation prioritising safety outcomes: specifically 3 commercial transcription-systems (Dragon-Medical-One, Heidi-Health, Tortus); 4 ASR speech-to-text Application Programming Interfaces (Speechmatics-Enhanced, Amazon-Medical-Transcribe, Whisper, GPT4oTranscribe); and an experimental two-stage ASR–Large Language Model (LLM) pipeline incorporating GPT4oTranscribe with GPT-5-LLM generative error correction (GPT4oTranscribe-Corrected-5). Reference-transcripts ( n = 100; 32,897 words, range = 44–449, mean = 329/per-transcript) derived from surgical case-reports were recorded and input into AVT systems as audio-recordings for transcription-output generation. Primary outcome was proportion of transcription-outputs containing at least one clinically significant Class 3 error graded for potential harm. Secondary outcomes included transcription accuracy: Domain-Word-Error-Rate (DWER) against SNOMED-CT, lexical-accuracy (ROUGE score) and semantic similarity (BERT, BART scores). title: Development and Nationwide Multicentre Evaluation of Guideline-Grounded Large Language Model Chatbots to Support Patient Self-Management and Education in Rheumatology
abstract: Patients with rheumatic diseases have persistent information needs that are not fully addressed in routine care. We developed and evaluated guideline-grounded, large language model (LLM) chatbots to support patient self-management and education in rheumatology. Ten disease-specific chatbots based on German guidelines were co-developed and deployed through 13 rheumatology centres and six patient organisations. Chatbot users rated responses and completed a questionnaire. User questions, feedback, and response characteristics were analysed using category-based coding and a six-dimensional LLM-as-a-judge assessment, with LLM-based ratings compared with rheumatologist ratings in random subsets. Between September 2025 and January 2026, 6291 questions were recorded. Thirteen question categories were identified, most commonly disease-specific questions (50.2%), medication and monitoring (37.3%) and diagnostics (28.2%). The chatbots were unable to answer in 263 interactions (4.2%). Of 2671 responses rated by users, 2481 (92.9%) received a positive rating. Insufficient detail was the most common reason for negative ratings (125/190, 65.8%). Among 602 questionnaire respondents, 84.6% reported that the chatbot was easy to use, 84.1% that answers were easy to understand, and 80.2% that it was a useful addition to patient education. In the LLM-based evaluation, 95.3% of answers were rated as completely safe and 79.1% as completely correct. Guideline adherence was assessed separately, with 45.0% rated as fully adherent; agreement with physician assessment was weak. Guideline-grounded chatbots received predominantly positive user feedback in real-world use, while LLM-based evaluation suggested that most responses were safe and correct. User questions and feedback may help guide iterative improvements to source content and patient education materials. Further studies are needed to evaluate educational effectiveness and independently validate response quality and clinical safety.

title: Co-developing equity-oriented neighbourhood care for children and young people with multiple long-term conditions: a concept mapping study in South London
abstract: Abstract Children and young people (CYP) with multiple long-term conditions (MLTCs) rely on services spanning health, education, and social care, but fragmented pathways may widen inequalities and shift coordination work to families. We aimed to identify priorities for equity-oriented neighbourhood care. We conducted a participatory mixed-methods study informed by the Medical Research Council framework and group concept mapping. Sixteen stakeholders participated: three CYP, seven parents, five healthcare professionals (HCPs), and one community stakeholder. Participants generated, sorted, and rated candidate components. Group data were analysed separately using multidimensional scaling and hierarchical cluster analysis, then synthesised through stakeholder interpretation and consensus. The Rainbow Model of Integrated Care informed interpretation. HCPs and community stakeholders refined 38 candidate neighbourhood-care statements to 27 and generated five clusters; families refined 52 candidate neighbourhood-care statements to 36 and generated four clusters. Seven priorities were co-developed: tailored information, local access, and pathway communication; named coordination; workforce capability; shared care-planning tools; multidisciplinary working; parent/carer support; and embedded mental health support. Communication, local access, and navigation were relatively feasible, whereas mental health and cross-sector integration were resource-dependent. A stakeholder-informed programme theory linked components to accountability, information-sharing, culturally responsive care, earlier escalation, and reduced family burden. The findings translate neighbourhood-care policy into co-developed, equity-oriented priorities for CYP with MLTCs in South London. Communication, local access, and coordination offer practical starting points, while mental health and cross-sector integration require phased resourcing and leadership. These priorities may inform adaptation in European child health systems.

title: Large language model–based classification of adverse event severity: agreement with final human classification in a single-center study
abstract: Background Adverse event (AE) reporting systems are central to hospital safety monitoring, yet severity classification remains dependent on human review and may be subject to variability among reviewers. Large language models (LLMs) may support more consistent classification of safety reports. Objective To evaluate agreement between a large language model (LLM)-based classification system and adjudicated expert human classifications of adverse event (AE) severity, while characterizing variability in the human classification process. Methods We analyzed 286 adverse event reports from the institutional safety reporting system of a tertiary academic medical center. Two quality and safety experts independently classified each report according to an A–I severity scale aligned with the National Coordinating Council for Medication Error Reporting and Prevention (NCC MERP) framework; disagreements were adjudicated by a third senior reviewer to establish the final human classification. The same reports were processed by a prespecified LLM-based workflow whose configuration was fixed before evaluation, without training, fine-tuning, calibration, or prompt modification on the study dataset; when the workflow generated clarification questions, the recorded responses were used to produce a second classification. Exact agreement with the final human classification was treated as the primary descriptive agreement measure; one-category differences and larger discordances were considered separately. Results Initial exact agreement between the two human reviewers was 65.4% (187/286), with moderate inter-rater reliability (unweighted Cohen’s κ = 0.563; linear weighted κ = 0.740). The final LLM classification exactly matched the final human classification in 140 of 286 cases (49.0%); 125 (43.7%) differed by one category within the prespecified A–E near-match range, and 21 (7.3%) were larger discordances. Linear weighted Cohen’s κ was 0.728 (bootstrap 95% CI, 0.678–0.770). Among severe-harm cases (F–I, n = 48), 37 (77.1%) were exact matches and 11 (22.9%) were mismatches. Human reviewers spent approximately 61 cumulative hours on classification, whereas AI inference required 4 min and 47 s. Conclusions In this single-center study, an LLM-based system showed meaningful ordinal agreement with adjudicated expert severity classification, but clinically important discordances were concentrated toward under-classification. The findings support further evaluation of LLM-assisted severity classification as supervised decision support rather than autonomous adjudication. Prospective, multicenter, and independently validated studies are needed.

title: Designing of specialized language model for medical diagnosis: a systematic review of architectures, applications, and clinical challenges
abstract: Background Large Language Models have become impactful in medicine by facilitating the processing of difficult medical data and aiding diagnosis-making. Given general LLM’s weaknesses, specialized medical LLMs are constructed for clinical precision, contextual understanding and safety in risky diagnostic applications. This review summarizes recent trends in medical LLMs for diagnosis, reported during 2021–2025. Methods A systematic literature review was performed following the PRISMA methodology. A search was designed and systematically carried out in the SCOPUS database using criteria of inclusion and exclusion (type of publication, language, period and country) and 75 peer-reviewed articles were chosen from a database of 1,911 records, after a multi-stage screening and eligibility evaluation. Results In summary, there have been significant advancements in the design and application of medical LLMs, with trends in hybrid architecture, multi-modal learning, prompt optimization techniques, diffusion-based imaging models, and multi-agent diagnostic system models. However, a number of persistent challenges that need to be overcome remain in the development and implementation of these models; namely, hallucination, bias, and poor probability calibration in LLMs, issues with explainability of LLMs, and ineffectiveness in a clinical environment. Conclusions This review highlights the fast pace of development and limitations of domain-specific medical LLMs. While impressive improvements in diagnostic performance have been made, the future directions must address improvements in reliability, safety and clinical validation in order to be seamlessly and responsibly incorporated in the practice.

title: Fragmented Care and Unmet Needs: A Multi-methods Study of Sexual and Reproductive Health Services in Libya
abstract: Objectives Prolonged conflict and political instability have severely strained Libya’s healthcare system, creating significant gaps in sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services. We aimed to assess the availability and accessibility of comprehensive SRH services in three regions of Libya and identify avenues for improvement. Methods We conducted this multi-methods qualitative study in Benghazi, Sabha, and Tripoli. Our research included a desk review, a service mapping exercise, 16 in-depth interviews with women of reproductive age, nine focus group discussions involving 60 women, and 11 key informant interviews with healthcare providers, policymakers, and non-governmental organization representatives. We analyzed these data for content and themes using deductive and inductive techniques and triangulated the results. Results Sexual and reproductive health services are centralized in urban hospitals, leading to overcrowding and limited access in other geographic areas. Although pregnancy and delivery services are available, family planning programs are limited, emergency contraception is virtually absent, and abortion services are restricted to life-threatening cases. Cultural stigma, workforce shortages, disorganized referrals, and government hostility exacerbate barriers to care. Many women turn to the private sector, which is costly and often inadequate for their complex needs. Conclusions for Practice We highlight critical gaps in Libya’s SRH service delivery landscape, driven by systemic, infrastructural, and cultural barriers. Decentralizing services, strengthening referral systems, addressing cultural stigma, and improving government responsiveness are essential for advancing equitable access to SRH care and improving health outcomes for Libyan women. Future research should explore long-term strategies to address these challenges in this conflict-affected and fragile setting.

title: Frontline Perspectives: WIC Clinic Emergency Preparedness Following Hurricane Helene
abstract: Introduction The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) targets nutrition and health behaviors of high-risk populations. WIC is administered by the U.S. Department of Agriculture and provides services in 4 areas: nutrition education, breastfeeding promotion and support, healthy food access, and healthcare and social services referrals. Methods To better understand services provided and populations served during Hurricane Helene and document personal and organizational preparedness, data were collected via an online survey. Descriptive statistics were used to characterize respondents. Odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated for associations between self-assessed preparedness and need for additional training. Results Of 95 WIC contacts, 29 responded (30.5%). Of four key WIC services, breastfeeding support was most frequently disrupted (43.5%; n = 10), followed by health care and social service referrals (39.1%; N = 9). Respondents characterized rural residents (47.8%; n = 11) and new clients seeking services (39.1%; n = 9) as most impacted. Respondents with confidence in their organization’s ability to respond to a disaster or in their personal knowledge of disaster preparedness were less likely to want additional training. Qualitative responses described challenges providing services to evacuated clients, food security, and internet outages. Discussion Disaster research has identified “gendered disaster vulnerability” as a challenge in emergency preparedness and response. Women and children often face intersectional risks from poverty, social marginalization, and disability in disasters. As such, the WIC workforce should be considered first responders and have access to emergency preparedness planning and training resources at the organizational and individual level.

title: Investigating the Relationship Between Highly Collaborative Local Health Jurisdictions and County-Level Perinatal Health Outcomes
abstract: Objectives Clarifying how cross-sector collaboration relates to perinatal health outcomes is essential in establishing tools to improve maternal and infant health. This study aims to establish if residence in a highly collaborative local health jurisdiction relates to one’s probability of experiencing poor perinatal health outcomes. Methods We measured collaboration between local health departments and social service organizations using data from the 2018 National Longitudinal Survey of Public Health Systems (NALSYS). We then used Latent Class Analysis to identify high and low collaborating counties, followed by multiple logistic regressions to assess the probability of six selected perinatal health outcomes among those residing in high and low collaborating counties at the time of labor and delivery. Health outcome data was selected from the 2018 National Vital Statistics System (NVSS) data. Results Using a national sample of local health departments across the United States, we found significant racial differences in the association between residence in a high collaborating county and the probability of poor perinatal health outcomes. White women experienced a lower probability of poor perinatal health outcomes if they resided in a high versus a low collaborating county, whereas the inverse was true for Black women. When stratified by payer, privately insured individuals had a lower risk of gestational diabetes if they resided in a high collaborating county, whereas those covered by Medicaid saw little to no effect. Conclusions for Practice These results suggest that local health jurisdictions should give greater attention to the needs of historically marginalized populations when planning and implementing collaborative activities to address community health needs.

title: An analytical and machine learning approach to evaluating economic impacts of digital transformation
abstract: Digital transformation has become a significant driver of economic and social development in the twenty-first century, producing both positive and negative economic repercussions. It involves the strategic integration of digital technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, and the Internet of Things (IoT), across business, government, and societal functions to transform operations, enhance value creation, improve adaptability, and support long-term sustainability. This study examines the relationship between digital transformation, AI-driven technological development, economic repercussions, and technology-bubble dynamics. Key findings: AI and digital transformation have emerged as important concerns for economists, policymakers, and technology-driven organizations. Generative AI is increasingly evolving from an emerging technology into a strategic tool for decision-making, while effective data strategies have become central to successful digital transformation. In developing economies, digital transformation provides opportunities to address developmental barriers, industrialization challenges, poverty, educational inequalities, and limited healthcare access. However, the shortage of skilled professionals capable of implementing and managing advanced technologies remains a significant challenge. Methods: This study reviews and comparatively analyses machine learning, deep learning, and advanced analytical methods used to evaluate economic repercussions associated with digital transformation. The analysis considers computational cost, time complexity, efficiency, economic outcomes, investment behaviour, and technology-related risks. Particular attention is given to the evolution of technology bubbles, including Tech Bubble 1.0 (Dot-Com), Tech Bubble 2.0 (Post-2008/COVID-19), and Tech Bubble 3.0 (AI and emerging technologies). Conclusion: Digital transformation is not a one-time technological initiative but a continuous process of organizational and economic adaptation. The study identifies major developments, methodological trends, economic implications, opportunities, challenges, and potential technology-bubble risks, providing insights into sustainable digital transformation and future AI-driven economic development.

title: Reducing demographic inequality in emergency medical service: two bi-objective spatial optimization approaches
abstract: Background Population demographic structures have become increasingly complex worldwide, posing new challenges for planning Emergency Medical Services (EMS) in ways to improve equality. Existing geographical studies have mainly focused on EMS equality in geographic accessibility or coverage, while demographic equality has received less attention. This study develops spatial optimization models that incorporate demographic equality into facility location planning. Methods Two bi-objective spatial optimization models are developed to improve demographic equality, while maintaining efficiency provision of EMS. In detail, the two models have the same efficiency objective that is to maximize the service coverage ( Z 1 ). Then, the first model (M1) addresses coverage-based demographic equality by minimizing disparities in coverage rates among population groups ( Z 2 ). The second model (M2) focused on accessibility-based demographic equality by minimizing the maximum average travel time among demographic groups ( Z 3 ). The models were applied to Wuhan, China, using age groups as the demographic representation and historical emergency medical service records to estimate spatially varying age-specific risks. Results The empirical results showed that both models were effective in improving demographic equality, although clear trade-offs were observed between equality enhancement and service efficiency. For M1, the nine Pareto-optimal solutions indicated that coverage-based demographic inequality, measured by Z 2 , decreased from 7.64% to 0.61%. This improvement in demographic equality, however, required an efficiency loss of up to 3.94% of total coverage. For M2, improving accessibility for the worst-served demographic group by 1.4 min ( Z 3 ) required a remarkable trade-off. The equality-oriented solution requires a 3.98% of efficiency loss compared with the efficiency-oriented solution. Both models consistently identified southern Hongshan and northern Jiangxia as priority areas for new EMS stations. Conclusions The proposed framework provides a transferable approach for integrating population-group equality into healthcare planning and supports more equitable allocation of EMS resources.

title: Air pollution-related health vulnerability index assessment: a multidimensional approach highlighting socio-spatial inequalities in urban Dakar
abstract: Background Ambient air pollution is an increasingly pressing public health concern in West African cities. In the Dakar metropolitan area (Senegal), socio-spatial inequalities in health vulnerability related to air pollution remain poorly documented, largely due to the lack of comprehensive, disaggregated data, which are often available only at spatial scales too coarse to reflect local disparities. Objective This study aims to assess socio-spatial disparities in health vulnerability to ambient air pollution in two municipalities of Dakar: Hann Bel-Air and HLM. It seeks to identify neighbourhood-level vulnerability patterns to inform place-based public health strategies. Methods A composite health vulnerability index was developed using a multidimensional framework integrating three components: proxy-based residential exposure, derived from traffic-related indicators and population density, health sensitivity, and adaptive capacity. The index was constructed through min–max normalisation and equal aggregation of normalized indicators and was spatialised at the neighbourhood level using household survey data combined with secondary demographic, transport and environmental indicators. Results The results show that high levels of vulnerability are concentrated in densely populated neighbourhoods characterized by high levels of socio-economic insecurity, particularly along major roads and in areas resulting from the fragmentation of traditional village structures in Hann Bel-Air. Conversely, in some residential estates with more affluent populations, vulnerability is lower, even when higher proxy-based exposure scores or health problems are reported, due to a greater adaptive capacity that provides protection against pollution-related effects. Conclusions The spatialised vulnerability index developed in this study demonstrates the value of incorporating exposure, health sensitivity, and adaptive capacity to capture fine-grained socio-spatial disparities. This study’s findings offer an innovative analytical framework to support targeted interventions and context-specific public health planning in urban African settings. It emphasises the importance of addressing both environmental hazards and the social determinants of health, while accounting for locally situated resilience capacities.

title: Assessing the spatial alignment between AED supply and spatiotemporal cardiac arrest risk in Beijing: a multi-source geospatial analysis
abstract: Background Automated External Defibrillators (AEDs) are critical medical devices for managing out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). Their life-saving efficiency depends heavily on the precision of their spatial allocation. However, influenced by population aging and urban functional evolution, existing AED deployments are often biased toward public buildings and large transportation hubs. This results in an incomplete spatial alignment between supply and the actual, localized demand for cardiac arrest intervention. Methods Drawing on Spatial Mismatch Theory and Ecosystem Service Supply-Demand Matching logic, this study proposes a multi-source geospatial data-driven framework for supply-demand assessment. We integrated high-resolution population grids, points of interest (POIs), and nighttime light imagery to construct a composite risk index, encompassing elderly population vulnerability, public activity-induced risk, and nighttime residential aggregation risk. AED supply accessibility was evaluated using road network topology based on the 4-minute total emergency response window, corresponding to a 3-minute effective accessibility threshold after accounting for approximately 1 min of AED operation time. Finally, a deployment priority index, was developed to identify emergency service “blind spots” through non-linear superposition. Results AED deployment in Beijing’s core urban area exhibits a pronounced “function-oriented” pattern, with high coverage in commercial centers and transportation hubs but structural supply gaps in high-risk residential zones. The comprehensive risk of cardiac arrest follows a “core-concentration and axial-extension” structure. Elderly population vulnerability is the primary driver of risk heterogeneity and carries the highest weight (0.3756). A Global Bivariate Moran’s I of -0.496 confirms a significant negative spatial autocorrelation between risk and supply gap. Local Bivariate LISA analysis identified multiple “High-Demand, High-Gap” (H-H) emergency blind spots, which represent critical nodes requiring prioritized “gap-filling” reinforcement. Conclusion This study demonstrates that as foundational AED coverage reaches a phased milestone, the marginal utility of a “blanket deployment” mode solely pursuing scale expansion is diminishing. The observed incomplete spatial alignment between existing resources and the shifting risk landscape underscores the structural necessity of transitioning from a “facility-oriented” to a “people-oriented” planning paradigm. The transition toward precision reinforcement in identified high-risk areas represents a cost-effective pathway to enhance spatial coordination and health equity.

title: Bridging concessional-loan and grant-linked aid for global health: a qualitative content analysis of Korea’s blended-aid model
abstract: Background Integrated loan-and-grant aid models are increasingly promoted as a means of addressing fragmentation in global health. However, empirical evidence on how these complex aid models function in the real world remains limited. This study explored how the outcomes and structural constraints of Korea’s Concessional-loan and Grant-linked Aid (CGA) model are represented within institutional evaluation processes. Methods This study employed qualitative content analysis of eight end-of-project evaluation reports of CGA projects in the healthcare sector, implemented across six low- and middle-income countries between 2015 and 2025. Treating the evaluation reports as policy artefacts, we applied a sequential hybrid analytical approach, combining inductive thematic coding with deductive mapping onto the WHO Health System Building Blocks as system domains and the OECD-DAC Evaluation Criteria as evaluative lenses. A total of 73 text segments were analysed across the eight reports. Results The evaluation narratives consistently highlighted immediate, facility-level operational gains, particularly in terms of service delivery, workforce capacity, and medical technology utilisation. However, a recurring pattern of ‘conditional success’ emerged, wherein these achievements coexisted with persistent structural vulnerabilities. The analysis identified critical ‘timeline mismatches’ between the rapid deployment of capital infrastructure through concessional loans and the more gradual processes of human capacity-building through grants. Furthermore, the narratives portrayed long-term system integration as constrained by high staff turnover and limited domestic fiscal capacity for ongoing maintenance. Conclusions The evaluation narratives suggested that, within the studied cases, operational improvements associated with blended-aid arrangements coexisted with continuing challenges to sustained health system integration. They portrayed such integration as contingent not only on financial alignment but also on the coordination of implementation timelines and capacity-development cycles. The findings support considering project-level mechanisms for cross-agency coordination and post-project continuity during early-stage project planning and host-country arrangements. Ultimately, the evaluation narratives highlight the value of reflexive approaches that examine underlying structural constraints alongside reported project-level achievements. title: MRI-to-CT Translation of Spinal Images via Anatomy-Guided Pseudo-Pairing and Adversarial Diffusion
abstract: arXiv:2610.37134v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is routinely used to diagnose spinal disorders, but surgical planning often requires Computed Tomography (CT) for better visualization of vertebral bone anatomy. Synthesizing CT from MRI could avoid additional radiation exposure and streamline preoperative assessment. We propose a three-stage framework for spine MRI-to-CT synthesis. First, an anatomy-guided vertebral matching system identifies similar sagittal MRI and CT slices using spine segmentations and aligns them through rigid registration, creating pseudo-paired data from unpaired scans. Second, these pairs train an adversarial diffusion model for MRI-to-CT translation. Third, synthesized slices are assembled into 3D volumes and refined by a network that improves inter-slice continuity and structural coherence. The framework was trained on over 10,000 unpaired sagittal MRI and CT slices and evaluated on 1,911 slices from 83 MRI volumes spanning all spinal regions. Assessment combined distribution-based measures with vertebral segmentation metrics. Compared with diffusion alone, the proposed approach increased binary 3D vertebral Dice from 0.666 to 0.739. Volumetric post-processing reduced visible discontinuities between stacked slices and improved vertebral coherence in axial and coronal views. Combining anatomy-guided pseudo-pairing, adversarial diffusion and 3D refinement improves spine MRI-to-CT synthesis. Vertebral matching primarily enhanced anatomical alignment and fidelity, while volumetric refinement improved 3D consistency. These findings support further development of MRI-derived CT-like visualization for preoperative planning, particularly to preserve fine intensity details while maintaining volumetric coherence.

title: Spatio-temporal machine learning for multi-horizon prediction of bluetongue outbreaks
abstract: by Lucy M. Devlin, Phi H. Nguyen, Ross N. Cuthbert, Phu Ngoc Doan, Viet Hung Tran, Zichi Zhang, Archie K. Murchie, Connor G. G. Bamford, Jaimie T. A. Dick, Eric R. Morgan, Thai S. Mai Reliable early warning of infectious disease outbreaks remains a major challenge for surveillance systems, particularly for vector-borne pathogens whose transmission depends on interactions among hosts, vectors, and climate-sensitive environmental conditions. Data-driven forecasting offers a promising approach for predicting outbreak risk using surveillance and environmental data. This study develops a logit-weighted ensemble (LWE), a machine-learning framework that predicts outbreak occurrence 1–6 months ahead at the administrative unit–month scale using routinely available outbreak notifications and gridded climate data. Bluetongue virus (BTV), an arbovirus of ruminants transmitted by Culicoides biting midges, provides a well-characterised system in which transmission is strongly shaped by climate, making it a useful system for applying and testing this approach. The framework is evaluated using surveillance data collected between 2005 and 2024 from France, Greece, and Italy, selected for their long-running and high-quality outbreak surveillance records. Across all three countries, the LWE achieved the strongest and most stable predictive performance under a recall-focused evaluation that prioritises correctly identifying outbreak months. It outperformed or matched 14 benchmark models, with differences becoming more pronounced at longer lead times (month +3 onward), when predictions are more uncertain and outbreaks are relatively rare. Predictability varied across countries, with the highest performance in Greece, strong performance in France, and lower, more variable performance in Italy, reflecting differences in how consistently outbreaks occur and spread across regions. Overall, the results demonstrate that horizon-aware, climate-informed forecasting can reliably identify months and locations at elevated risk of outbreak occurrence up to six months in advance, supporting surveillance planning and preparedness across heterogeneous European settings. The ensemble framework provides a robust and portable strategy for outbreak prediction using routinely collected surveillance and environmental data.

title: Impression-regularized finetuning enables small language models to extract cervical spine fractures from radiology reports
abstract: by Zixuan Hu, Hui Ming Lin, Yingming Amy Chen, Christopher S. Lozano, Markand Patel, Ali Emami, Ervin Sejdić, Errol Colak We assessed whether small, open-weight large language models (LLMs) can accurately extract vertebral-level acute cervical spine fracture labels from CT radiology reports while supporting on-premises deployment, and whether impression-regularized finetuning improves accuracy, data efficiency, and temporal stability. In this single-center retrospective study, 8,567 adult cervical spine CT reports (2017–2022) were labeled for acute occipital condyle and C1–C7 fractures with neuroradiologist oversight. Reports from 2017 (n = 1,064) were used for finetuning and reports from 2018–2022 (n = 7,503) for temporal testing. We finetuned Gemma-3 (1B/4B/12B), Llama-3.2-3B, and Phi-3.5-Mini using standard low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and with an impression-regularized LoRA approach. During training, the model samples multiple synthetic targeted impressions focused on acute cervical spine fractures, selects the candidate most consistent with the reference standard labels, and applies an auxiliary impression loss as regularization. At inference, all models perform single-pass deterministic JSON extraction. Baselines included zero-shot prompting, two-pass impression-guided prompting, and standard LoRA. Impression-regularized LoRA improved Gemma-3-4B macro-F1 from 0.885 to 0.909 (macro-precision 0.929, macro-recall 0.893) while reducing variance across training runs. Improvements were largest for smaller models and in low-data settings; Gemma-3-1B macro-F1 increased from 0.646 to 0.782. For this vertebral-level acute cervical spine fracture extraction task, impression-regularized Gemma-3-4B approached the zero-shot performance of the Gemma-3-27B (macro-F1 0.909 vs. 0.913). Across the 2018–2022 temporal evaluation, mean F1 increased from 0.871 to 0.893 with similar or lower variability across time windows. Systematic error analysis showed that remaining errors were mainly associated with ambiguous report language and label-boundary cases. Overall, impression-regularized LoRA enables small open-weight LLMs to accurately extract acute cervical spine fracture labels while maintaining performance across a multi-year test period and preserving auditable single-pass inference suitable for privacy-preserving on-premises deployment.

title: Personalized physiotherapy effect modeling with continuous causal machine learning
abstract: IntroductionEstimating how physiotherapy (PT) intensity influences functional independence is central to personalized care planning for older adults. However, most existing causal inference approaches treat PT as a binary intervention, which requires collapsing a naturally continuous measure of treatment intensity and limits the ability to characterize nuanced dose–response relationships.MethodsTo address this limitation, we use continuous causal inference to estimate individualized continuous dose–response curves for PT. This approach enables granular assessment of treatment effects across therapy intensities and supports the identification of optimal treatment doses. The model is trained on Canadian Community Care data and externally validated using an independent Canadian Home Care cohort.ResultsAcross factual, proxy counterfactual, and external validation settings, our approach generally achieved lower prediction error on activities of daily living outcomes, as measured by root mean squared error (RMSE), than standard baselines. In particular, we attained factual and proxy counterfactual RMSEs of 3.79 and 3.89, respectively, compared with 4.09 and 6.49 for linear regression, while also demonstrating strong external generalization.ConclusionContinuous causal modeling of individualized dose–response relationships provides a principled approach to estimating physiotherapy intensity effects on functional independence, with direct implications for personalized rehabilitation planning in older adults.

title: Hybrid Multi-View MRI Fusion for csPCa Diagnosis via Intra- and Inter-View Transformers
abstract: Accurate diagnosis of clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) from multi-view MRI scans (axial, sagittal, coronal) is essential for effective treatment planning and improved outcomes. Although deep learning has advanced prostate MRI analysis, many approaches adopt late fusion strategies aggregating flattened features independently from each view, resulting in loss of spatial information and anatomical correspondence across views, ultimately limiting diagnostic performance. While Vision Transformers offer flexibility for multi-view patches, their memory requirements scale quadratically, hindering efficient concurrent processing. Conversely, Swin Transformers efficiently capture local features but are restricted to single-view processing due to regular-grid input constraints. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid fusion framework that decomposes multi-view integration into iterative intra-view and inter-view interactions across multiple resolutions. The framework preserves spatial coherence and enables fine-grained feature integration while maintaining computational efficiency. Specifically, the inter-view feature exchange module, based on the Vision Transformer, employs bridge tokens to summarize information from localized patch windows, reducing memory usage while preserving spatial relationships across views. The intra-view feature extraction module, built on the Swin Transformer, facilitates dynamic, attention-driven interactions among image patches and bridge tokens within each window. Moreover, shared positional embeddings are explicitly incorporated to enhance spatial correspondence across views. Extensive experiments on a public dataset demonstrate the superiority of our method in csPCa classification. Ablation studies highlight component contributions, while attention map visualizations validate integration of anatomical structures across views.

title: A Systematic Review of Human-in-the-Loop Adaptive Systems: Design, Implications, and Future Directions
abstract: Adaptive systems aim to address the human-out-of-the-loop problem in automation, associated with reduced situation awareness and users' overreliance. These systems modify their behavior based on system, task, or operator-based triggers, with the latter offering a human-centered approach by responding to different human states such as mental workload or fatigue. Despite growing interest in adaptive systems, no review has consolidated empirical findings. To fill this gap, and using PRISMA methodology, 34 articles were included after full-text screening. The analysis focuses on the types of human states measured, the sensors and modeling techniques used, the nature of the adaptive interventions, and their reported outcomes. Cognitive states were the most commonly assessed, often using EEG due to its ability to capture brain activity in real time. Physical state, frequently applied in rehabilitation, relied on EMG and IMU sensors to assess muscle activation and joint accuracy. Machine learning methods were more prevalent than rule-based systems, likely due to their flexibility and robustness. While function allocation emerged as the dominant adaptive strategy, system performance outcomes varied. Future work should prioritize user-centered design, avoiding task disruption or disengagement. Finally, standardized evaluation frameworks are required to assess human–machine performance.

title: Nosocomial outbreak of Ralstonia mannitolilytica associated with prefilled saline flush syringes distributed in Europe, Germany, March to September 2026
abstract: A nosocomial outbreak of Ralstonia mannitolilytica bloodstream infections in Germany from March to September 2026 included 16 cases (≤ 6 allelic differences using core genome multilocus sequence typing) across seven hospitals. Epidemiological investigations supported by a large language model, identified prefilled saline flush syringes of one manufacturer as common exposure across all cases. The manufacturer initiated a temporary quarantine and suspension of use of this product. Because it was distributed to other countries, cases may have occurred elsewhere, prompting this report.
